correctness.rationale: The claim was reconstructed independently from the exact package. A fresh implementation enumerated all \(6^6=46656\) strict labelled profiles, tested all six perfect matchings for stability, and then formed full orbits under independent relabelling of each side together with side exchange. It reproduced raw counts \(34080,11484,1092\), exactly \(491,161,17\) full-symmetry classes for one, two, and three stable matchings, hence \(669\) classes total, and three-stable orbit sizes \(72^{\times14},36^{\times2},12^{\times1}\). The assigned verifier independently implements generator-orbit partitioning and a separate Burnside fixed-profile count over all \(72\) group elements, and its expected values match the fresh reconstruction.

originality.rationale: The complete primary stable-matching sequence paper gives the labelled distribution for the \(3\)-by-\(3\) problem and explicitly discusses the relevant relabelling and side-exchange symmetries, but its symmetry section quotients more limited profile data and does not give the full two-sided \((S_3\times S_3)\rtimes C_2\) orbit census, orbit-size distribution, or stabilizers. OEIS A344666 likewise gives only the labelled stable-matching-count distribution. A Resultary search for the exact full-symmetry census did not return a prior equivalent record among the relevant hits. The published labelled counts plus knowledge of the symmetry group do not determine the orbit counts without fixed-point/orbit information, so the submitted complete quotient census is not a direct corollary of the inspected sources.
residual_risks: A separate stable-marriage isomorphism-class catalogue using the identical full symmetry group could exist under different terminology, although none was located in the targeted searches.

value.rationale: The \(3\)-by-\(3\) case is the first size with a nontrivial distribution up to three stable matchings, and the primary literature already singles out its labelled sequence and symmetry operations. A complete quotient by the natural full symmetry group, including stabilizer strata, is therefore a motivated finite classification rather than an arbitrary sample. The result separates genuinely different profile types that the known raw count does not distinguish.
